items.title: Section: The Three Purities Open — A Standing Method for Examining Body, Speech, and Mind

items.zh: 又戒律儀有三種觀清淨因相。何等為三？一、觀身業，二、觀語業，三、觀意業。云何觀察如是諸業，令戒律儀皆得清淨？謂希當造及欲正造身作業時，如是觀察：我此身業為能自損，及以損他，是不善性，能生眾苦，招苦異熟？為不自損，亦不損他，是其善性，能生諸樂，招樂異熟？如是觀已。若自了知我此身業，自損損他，是不善性，能生眾苦，招苦異熟；即於此業攝斂不作，亦不與便。若自了知我此身業，不損自他，是其善性，餘如前說；即於此業而不攝斂、造作、與便。復於過去已造身業亦數觀察：我此身業為能自損，餘如前說。如是觀已。若自了知我此身業，自損損他，餘如前說；便於有智同梵行所，如實發露，如法悔除。若自了知我此身業，不損自他，餘如前說；便生歡喜，晝夜安住，多隨修學。如是彼於去來今世所造身業，能善觀察、能善清淨。如於身業，於其語業，當知亦爾。由過去行為緣生意，由未來行為緣生意，由現在行為緣生意，即於此意數數觀察：我此意業為能自損，餘如前說。如是觀已。若自了知我此意業是其黑品，即於此業攝斂不起，不與其便。若自了知我此意業是其白品，即於此業而不斂攝、發起、與便。如是於彼去來今世所起意業，能善觀察、能善清淨。所以者何？去來今世所有沙門、若婆羅門，於身語意三種業中，或已觀察、或當觀察、或正觀察，或已清淨、或當清淨、或正清淨，或已多住、或當多住、或正多住，一切皆由如是觀察、如是清淨。如佛世尊、曾為長老羅怙羅說：汝今羅怙羅！於身語意業，應數正觀察；念諸佛聖教。羅怙羅！汝應學是沙門業。若能於此學，唯勝善，無惡。
items.en: Moral restraint has three ways of observing the causal marks of its own purity. What are the three? Observing bodily conduct; observing verbal conduct; observing mental conduct. …When one is about to undertake, or is actually undertaking, a bodily action, one observes thus: is this bodily action of mine one that harms myself and harms others, unwholesome by nature, giving rise to manifold suffering, bringing a painful ripened result? Or is it one that harms neither myself nor others, wholesome by nature, giving rise to manifold happiness, bringing a pleasant ripened result? Having observed in this way — if one recognises that this bodily action harms both self and other … one restrains oneself from this action, and gives it no opportunity. If one recognises that this bodily action harms neither self nor other … one does not restrain, but instead performs it, giving it every opportunity. One also repeatedly examines bodily actions already performed in the past … one then confesses truthfully before a wise fellow practitioner, and confesses it away in accordance with the Dharma. …one gives rise to joy, abides in it day and night, and cultivates it further, again and again. …"Rāhula, regarding your bodily, verbal, and mental conduct, you should repeatedly and correctly observe it, recollecting the sacred teaching of all buddhas. Rāhula, you should train in this recluse's task — if you are able to train in this, there will be only excellent good, and no evil."

items.zh: 若於如是身語意業審正思擇，我此諸業為能自損，廣說如前，是名觀察。若於一分攝斂不作，亦不與便，廣說乃至發露悔除。復於一分而不斂攝，造作與便，廣說乃至便生歡喜，晝夜安住，多隨修學。是名清淨。
items.en: If one thus carefully and correctly considers one's bodily, verbal, and mental actions — 'Are these actions of mine able to harm myself?' — and so on at length as before, this is called examination. If, with respect to one part, one restrains oneself and does not perform it, nor gives it any opportunity, and so on at length up to confessing and making amends; and if, with respect to another part, one does not restrain oneself but performs it and gives it opportunity, and so on at length up to giving rise to joy, abiding day and night and training in it often — this is called purity.

items.title: Ten Excellent Virtues: From Freedom of Regret to the Fulfilment of Every Wish

items.zh: 如是清淨尸羅律儀，應知有十功德勝利。何等為十？謂諸所有具戒士夫補特伽羅，自觀戒淨，便得無悔；無悔故歡；歡故生喜；由心喜故，身得輕安；身輕安故，便受勝樂；樂故心定，心得定故，能如實知、能如實見；實知見故，便能起厭；能起厭故，便得離染；由離染故，證得解脫；得解脫故，便自知見我已解脫，乃至我能於無餘依般涅槃界當般涅槃。如是所有具戒士夫補特伽羅，尸羅清淨增上力故，獲得無悔，漸次乃至能到涅槃。是名第一尸羅律儀功德勝利。復有所餘具戒士夫補特伽羅：於臨終時起如是念：我已善作身語意行，非我惡作身語意行，乃至廣說。若有其趣，作福業者、作善業者、作能救濟諸怖畏者之所應往，我於斯趣必定當往。如是獲得能往善趣第二無悔。由無悔恨所有士夫補特伽羅，名賢善死、賢善夭逝、賢善過往。
items.en: Such pure moral restraint should be known to have ten excellent virtues. …It is that any person possessing discipline, observing that discipline to be pure, thereby attains freedom from regret; from freedom of regret comes delight; from delight, joy arises; because the mind is joyful, the body attains ease; because the body is at ease, one then experiences excellent pleasure; because of that pleasure, the mind becomes concentrated; because the mind is concentrated, one is able to know and see things as they truly are; because of this true knowing and seeing, one is able to give rise to revulsion; because revulsion arises, one attains dispassion; because of dispassion, one realises liberation; because of liberation, one knows and sees for oneself, "I am liberated" — even, in time, "I shall attain final nirvāṇa within the realm of nirvāṇa without residue." …There is, further, a person possessing discipline who, at the time of death, gives rise to this thought: "I have done only good through body, speech, and mind — I have done no evil through body, speech, or mind" … "wherever those who perform meritorious deeds, wholesome deeds, and deeds that rescue others from fear are destined to go, there I too shall certainly go." …This is called the second freedom from regret, the attainment of a favourable rebirth. Because of this freedom from regret, such a person is called one who dies well, passes away well, and departs well.

items.zh: 是名第二尸羅律儀功德勝利。
items.en: This is called the second excellent virtue of moral restraint.

blocks.text: How does one keep discipline pure? By observing one's own actions, as the Buddha taught his son Rāhula. Then the benefits begin.

"Moral restraint has three ways of observing the causes of its purity: observing bodily, verbal, and mental conduct." Before an act, while doing it, after it: is it harmful to oneself or to others? If so, "one restrains oneself, and gives it no opportunity". Venerable Miào Jìng: one stops even the preliminaries.

The treatise cites the Buddha's words to Rāhula: "Regarding your bodily, verbal, and mental conduct, you should repeatedly and correctly observe it." Master Cháng Bǎi: bodily and verbal conduct follow mental conduct; the heart of pure discipline is purity of mind.

subs.head: The first virtue: freedom from regret

blocks.text: "Observing that discipline to be pure, one attains freedom from regret; from that comes delight; from delight, joy; the body attains ease; one experiences pleasure; the mind becomes concentrated; one knows and sees as it truly is." Master Cháng Bǎi: joy is somewhat stronger than delight. Venerable Miào Jìng: the "ease" here is not yet that of the absorptions.

This chain, from a clear conscience to insight, is found throughout the early scriptures. It shows why moral discipline comes first: not as a rule, but because a mind free of regret is the natural ground of concentration.

Pure discipline leads to rebirth in good destinies. Master Cháng Bǎi: the first virtue concerns decisive excellence, the second higher rebirth. On death he adds: dying young is not necessarily bad; what matters is how one lived.

quiz.q: What are the three observations that cause purity of discipline?
options: observing bodily, verbal, and mental conduct
quiz.why: "Moral restraint has three ways of observing the causal marks of its own purity: observing bodily, verbal, and mental conduct." Venerable Miào Jìng: discipline becomes pure through observation, so observation is called the cause of purity.

quiz.q: "When one wishes to do or is about to do" is rendered "about to undertake, or on the verge of actually undertaking." How does Venerable Miào Jìng distinguish them?
options: "will do" is the future, "doing" is the present — the English renders both as "about to"
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "wish" means I want to do this now. "Will do" and "doing" are future and present. The English "on the verge of" does not express "doing right now."

quiz.q: If, after observing, one recognises a bodily action harms self and others, what does the treatise say to do?
options: restrain oneself and not do it, giving it no opportunity — even the preparations stop
quiz.why: "One restrains oneself from this action, and gives it no opportunity." Venerable Miào Jìng: any deed has preliminaries before the act; here even the preliminaries are stopped — no opening is given.

quiz.q: Among the three kinds of conduct, which does Master Cháng Bǎi call the key to pure discipline?
options: mental conduct — bodily and verbal follow it; it governs all
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: bodily and verbal conduct follow mental conduct; mental conduct governs everything, so the main point of pure discipline is purity of mental conduct.

quiz.q: To whom does the Buddha address the verse urging repeated observation of body, speech, and mind?
options: Rāhula — observe your conduct repeatedly; train in the recluse's task, and there will be only good
quiz.why: "Rāhula, regarding your bodily, verbal, and mental conduct, you should repeatedly and correctly observe it… if you are able to train in this, there will be only excellent good, and no evil." Master Cháng Bǎi: to attain purity one must keep mindfulness by observing the three kinds of conduct.

quiz.q: The first virtue begins with seeing one's discipline as pure. What follows in sequence?
options: no regret → delight → joy → ease → pleasure → concentration → true knowing and seeing → revulsion → dispassion → liberation → knowing "I am liberated"
quiz.why: "Observing that discipline to be pure, one attains freedom from regret; from that comes delight; from delight, joy; the body attains ease; one experiences pleasure; the mind becomes concentrated; one knows and sees as things are; revulsion; dispassion; liberation." Master Cháng Bǎi: with a good foundation one can build a tower to the top floor.

quiz.q: "From no regret, delight; from delight, joy" — how does Master Cháng Bǎi distinguish delight and joy?
options: without regret the heart is glad — delight; from delight joy, a little stronger
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: with no regret, the heart is glad and delight arises; from delight, joy — joy is somewhat stronger than delight.
